note: verbatim final report of the hand-over agent, run 1 (instruction.md); 9 tool uses, 130 s

grounds.passage: 00_product.md: Primary actions row 'erase a customer's contact data' [S0.erase_row] with origin 'a repeated erasure is a no-op' (7fb4e3af, 2026-10-26)
grounds.why: The only State 0 text that answers an erasure of an erased Customer: 'returns it unchanged'. The commit message gives its intent: a repeated erasure is a no-op. It was written a day before R0-35, so the owner never ruled on how it interacts with revisions.

It refuses 'a change against an older revision'. It is the source of every staleness rule. Its wording ('a change', 'older') assumes there is a current revision to compare with, and it does not by itself say what happens when there is none.

grounds.passage: 00_product.md: R0-06 ('nothing else'), R0-67; 01_models.md M04 erased mark and the read of an erased Customer
grounds.why: An erased Customer keeps no revision, and so no record of the revision it was erased from. Any answer that tells 'erased from 2' apart from any other number would need a fact these texts forbid.
State 0 refusals on an erased Customer. They fix the 'erased' answer when an action reaches the lifecycle check. Which answer comes first, stale or erased, is left to State 2's ordering.

grounds.passage: 00_product.md: R0-71, R0-62, 'erase an archived project' row; 01_models.md M01 (anonymised project has no revision)
grounds.why: The same no-revision situation for projects. Anonymising again returns the project unchanged and deleting it whole is refused. These fix W14 and W15, and they constrain W11 and W13.
Gives State 2 the choice of which actions state a revision. Whether it also covers how a revision stated against a record without one is answered is not said explicitly.

Erasing a customer is not a confirmed action, so a resubmitted customer erasure passes stage 1 and reaches stages 5 and 6. Erasing a project is confirmed, so its resubmission in the same session stops at stage 1 (W12). That leaves the customer erasure as the one case where this choice shows in the answer.

grounds.passage: 02_rules_records.md: A04 rules 1-3, the invariant, test 3 and the Consequence
grounds.why: r1: erasure states a revision and leaves none behind. r2: a stated revision that is not the current one is stale. r3: a no-change action still states the revision and is refused when stale, but a record without a revision 'states none'. The invariant 'stated != r.revision => refused' does not define the case where r.revision is absent. The Consequence (the UI sends the rendered card's revision) is what turns W01 from hypothetical into the normal resubmission.

grounds.passage: 02_rules_records.md: A04 rule 6 (stage order, 'a stage that does not apply to it is skipped'), A04 test 4
grounds.why: Stage (5), revision, comes before stage (6), lifecycle. Test 4 sets a precedent: 'stale, not archived'. The skip clause, though, allows reading stage (5) as not applying to a record that has no revision.

grounds.passage: 02_rules_records.md: A05 rules 1, 2, 4 and the Consequence; A01 Consequence
grounds.why: A repeat is accepted only after it passes all six stages. State 0 refusals 'stay refusals and come first'. 'A retried transition is safe' and 'a resubmitted owner form is safe' set the expectation for W01.
The confirmation is bound to 'the revision ... the step showed' and is used up whatever the answer. Several sessions make W02, W05, W07, W11 and W13 admissible.
Neither a refusal nor a no-change acceptance writes an entry. The audit log therefore does not separate the alternatives.

patch_check.detail: Accepted histories: all kept. W03, W04, W14 and W15 state none and are answered as State 0/A05 say. W07, W09 and W10 involve records that still have a revision. W08 states the current revision. W12 fails at stage 1 before the new text applies. Accepted passages: the S0 erase row is kept only literally, by reading 'erasing an erased customer' as 'stating none'. By A04's Consequence, the form that erased a Customer sends the erased-from revision, so the actual resubmission is now refused as stale. That departs from the row's recorded intent ('a repeated erasure is a no-op') and gives a refusal where A01/A05 promise a safe resubmission. It is safe in effect, since nothing changes, but not in the answer the owner sees. Whether that still keeps S0.erase_row is an interpretation of an owner text, hence 'unsure'. One more point: the patch settles A04's invariant for an absent r.revision as 'mismatch'. Nothing accepted says so; it is the patch's own addition.

alternatives.name: A: stale (the patch)
alternatives.behaviour: Any revision stated against an erased Customer or an anonymised project fails stage 5. A resubmitted erasure is refused as stale and changes nothing. Restricting from a pre-erasure card is refused as stale, not erased. Stating none gives State 0/A05 answers.
alternatives.grounds: A04 r2 read as 'not the current one' with absence counted as different; the A04 invariant; the A04 test 4 precedent (stale before lifecycle); A04 r3 'still states ... refused when stale'.

alternatives.name: B: revision stage skipped
alternatives.behaviour: A record without a revision has no revision to check, so stage 5 does not apply and is skipped (A04 r6). The action goes to stage 6. A resubmitted erasure gets unchanged (A05, S0 row). Restrict, correct or end from an old card get refused as erased. W11 anonymise gets unchanged; W13 delete whole gets refused by R0-71.
alternatives.grounds: A04 r6 'a stage that does not apply to it is skipped'; S0.erase_row and its origin intent; A05 and A01 Consequences ('retried/resubmitted ... safe'); R0-35 speaks of an 'older revision' of 'a change', and neither exists here.

alternatives.name: C: invalid input
alternatives.behaviour: A04 r3 'an action on them states none' is read as an input constraint. A stated revision on a record without one fails stage 4 (values) as an invalid or unexpected value, before staleness and lifecycle. Stating none gives State 0/A05 answers.
alternatives.grounds: A04 r3 as a constraint; A04 r6 stage (4) values; A02 (malformed values refused as values).

alternatives.name: D: remember the erased-from revision (not open to the author)
alternatives.behaviour: A resubmission stating exactly the erased-from revision answers unchanged; any other revision is stale.
alternatives.grounds: Fits the origin intent best, but conflicts with R0-06 'nothing else' and M04, which drop the revision. Only the owner could reopen that.

patch_check.why_who: A, B and C all keep the accepted histories and every accepted passage taken literally. They differ only in the answer to a State 0 Primary-actions row, and the owner's two texts never met: the S0 erase row and its intent (2026-10-26) predate R0-35 (2026-10-27), and R0-35's wording does not reach a record with no revision or an action that changes nothing. RT.state2 gives State 2 'which actions must state the revision'. It does not give State 2 the power to turn State 0's 'returns it unchanged' for the normal resubmission into a refusal. D needs a change to R0-06/M04 that only the owner can make. If the owner has already accepted A04 r3's narrowing of the 'returns unchanged' rows by staleness (the archive precedent), the author could argue for A within that delegation. I could not determine that; see requests.

neighbours.what: S0 'erase a customer's contact data' row
neighbours.effect_of_edit: In practice it only answers erasure from a card read after the erasure. If the owner UI offers no erase action on an erased Customer's card (unknown), the row's 'unchanged' outcome becomes reachable only by a hand-made request.

neighbours.what: A01 Consequence ('a resubmitted owner form is safe') and A05 Consequence ('a retried transition is safe')
neighbours.effect_of_edit: Still safe in effect, since nothing changes and no audit entry is written. But the resubmitted erasure form now gets a refusal that suggests the erasure did not happen.
Implicitly defined for an absent r.revision as a mismatch. The invariant text is not changed to say so; the patch adds a rule but no invariant line.
The edit picks 'stage 5 applies and fails' over 'stage 5 does not apply'. Rule 6 is not amended, so the skip clause still reads as the opposite and invites alternative B.
New test 7 (stale before erased) extends that precedent consistently.

neighbours.what: A05 rule 4 ('State 0 refusals ... come first'), R0-71
neighbours.effect_of_edit: For W13 (delete an anonymised project whole, stating revision 3), the edit answers stale where R0-71 says 'refused'. That holds only if 'come first' means before the A05 repeat acceptance and not before stage 5. The edit relies on that reading without stating it.

neighbours.what: A13 rule 6 (confirmation bound to the revision the step showed)
neighbours.effect_of_edit: For W11 and W13 the stale refusal uses up the confirmation, and the step must be shown again. A step shown on an anonymised project binds 'the revision the step showed', which is none. A13 does not say what a binding to 'no revision' is. The edit leaves this gap.
Unaffected. A refusal and a no-change acceptance both write no entry.
No conflict found. A restart ends every owner session (A13), so old forms fail at stage 1. A restored Customer has a revision again, so a fresh erasure states it.

neighbours.what: Open histories W02, W05, W06, W11, W13
neighbours.effect_of_edit: All are settled as stale. W16 (missing revision on a record that has one) is untouched.

counterexamples.history: The owner erases Customer C from its card at revision 2. The answer is lost (network drop). The browser or the owner resubmits the same form in the same session with a valid CSRF value. Customer erasure needs no confirmation, so it reaches stage 5.
counterexamples.problem: Under the edit the answer is 'refused as stale, nothing changes', although the erasure took effect. The owner is told nothing changed and is invited to reload and retry. That is misleading for the one case the S0 row and its intent ('a repeated erasure is a no-op') were written for, and it reads against the A01 promise about resubmitted forms.

counterexamples.history: C erased from revision 2. A hand-made or old-tab request erases C stating 99, a revision C never had. Another request states 2, the revision it was erased from.
counterexamples.problem: Both are answered stale. 'Stale' claims the form was made against an older revision, but Registry keeps no revision to compare against (R0-06, M04). The answer is a guess, not a comparison. Not contradictory, but not grounded in R0-35's 'older revision'.

counterexamples.history: Project P archived at revision 3 and anonymised in session 2. Session 1 shows a fresh 'delete whole' step for P. Whether that step can be shown, and what revision it binds, is unclear: A13 binds 'the revision the step showed'. The submission states either 3 (old card) or none.
counterexamples.problem: Stating 3 gives stale under the edit. Stating none gives the R0-71 refusal. Read with A05 r4's 'come first' as before all of stage 5, R0-71 would win in both cases. The edited text does not exclude that reading, so the answer is ambiguous.

requests.need: Who accepted A04 rule 3's sentence 'an action that would change nothing ... still states the revision and is refused when it is stale' (owner or State 2 author), and whether the owner was shown that it narrows the State 0 'returns it unchanged' rows.
requests.to_decide: Whether the author may choose alternative A within an existing owner delegation, or the choice must go to the owner.

requests.need: Whether the owner interface (State 2/3 UI texts) offers 'erase contact data' on an erased Customer's card, and what it renders as that card's revision.
requests.to_decide: Whether, under the edit, the S0 erase row's 'unchanged' answer is reachable from the UI at all, or survives only for hand-made requests.

requests.need: The authoritative reading of A05 rule 4's 'come first': before the A05 repeat acceptance only, or before stage 5 of A04 rule 6.
requests.to_decide: Whether W13 is stale or refused by R0-71 under any of the alternatives.

requests.need: What A13 rule 6 binds for a confirmation step shown on a record without a revision.
requests.to_decide: Whether W11 and W13 can fail at stage 1 (binding) before the edit's stage-5 rule is reached.
